title: How America Can Counter Chinese Coercion
gist: Teaser excerpt of a piece by Theodore Bunzel, Edward Fishman and Addar Levi making the case for an economic security alliance to counter Chinese economic coercion. The available text recounts China's April 2025 retaliation against U.S. tariffs (matching levies plus rare-earth export controls) that rattled bond markets and forced a still-standing truce, and its November 2025 coercion of Japan after PM Sanae Takaichi's Taiwan remarks; the rest is paywalled.

themes.theme: China's economic arsenal against the U.S.

insights.claim: In April 2025, China retaliated against U.S. tariffs with matching across-the-board levies and export controls on rare-earth elements.
insights.speaker: Theodore Bunzel
insights.so_what: Rare-earth export controls are China's proven escalation lever; watch rare-earth supply chains in any new tariff round.
insights.quote: In April 2025, Beijing retaliated forcefully against U.S. tariffs, imposing matching across-the-board levies and export controls on rare-earth elements.
insights.locator: Over the past year and a half

insights.claim: The authors say China's 2025 counterpunch rattled bond markets and disrupted auto supply chains, forcing Washington to seek a truce with Beijing that still persists in late 2026.
insights.speaker: Theodore Bunzel
insights.so_what: The U.S.-China truce rests on demonstrated Chinese leverage over Treasuries and autos; its breakdown would be a cross-asset risk event.
insights.quote: This counterpunch rattled bond markets and disrupted auto supply chains, forcing Washington to seek a truce that persists to this day.
insights.locator: Over the past year and a half

insights.claim: Over the past year and a half, China has demonstrated the power of its economic arsenal against multiple countries, starting with the United States.
insights.speaker: Theodore Bunzel
insights.so_what: Economic coercion is now a core Chinese tool; geopolitical disputes increasingly translate into trade and supply shocks.
insights.quote: Over the past year and a half, China has shown the world the power of its economic arsenal—starting with the United States.
insights.locator: Over the past year and a half

insights.claim: After Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described a potential Chinese naval blockade of Taiwan as a 'survival-threatening situation' that could justify deploying Japan's Self-Defense Forces, Beijing in November 2025 imposed sweeping bans on Japan.
insights.speaker: Theodore Bunzel
insights.so_what: Political statements on Taiwan now trigger immediate Chinese economic penalties; Japanese exporters exposed to China carry this risk.
insights.quote: a potential Chinese naval blockade of Taiwan as a “survival-threatening situation”

insights.claim: The authors make the case for an economic security alliance among the United States and partners as the answer to Chinese economic coercion.
insights.speaker: Theodore Bunzel
insights.so_what: Watch for allied coordination mechanisms (collective retaliation, stockpiles) that could reshape supply-chain policy.
insights.quote: The Case for an Economic Security Alliance
